## How it works

- [statement] NautilusTrader describes startup reconciliation as aligning cached order and position state with venue reports, followed by continuous checks of in-flight orders, open orders, positions, and own order books. This is an operational state-consistency mechanism. (low confidence) — https://nautilustrader.io/docs/latest/concepts/live/ · keywords: Crypto bot strategy drift and shadow divergence monitoring
- [statement] Freqtrade issue 10801 records a historical report that restarting FreqAI with nonzero live_retrain_hours could zero historical prediction fields. The issue’s environment and reproduction steps identify the tested historical development build. This is evidence to check restart continuity when investigating apparent divergence, not a claim that the bug persists in current releases. (low confidence) — https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/issues/10801 · keywords: Crypto bot strategy drift and shadow divergence monitoring
- [statement] For a comparable live/backtest baseline, QuantConnect advises matching deployment dates and initial holdings and preserving state across live restarts. It also identifies indicator input prices, candle timestamps, implementation defaults, and warm-up periods as possible causes of indicator discrepancies. (low confidence) — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/live-trading/reconciliation · keywords: Crypto bot strategy drift and shadow divergence monitoring

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] A clean Freqtrade lookahead-analysis result cannot clear untriggered signal types: the documentation warns that it verifies only calculated trades, so incomplete signal coverage can produce a false negative. (low confidence) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/lookahead-analysis/ · keywords: Crypto bot strategy drift and shadow divergence monitoring
- [statement] Freqtrade documents false-positive lookahead-analysis results for strategies whose behavior depends on the full pairlist, and for limit orders with custom entry or exit pricing. Its documentation also says that FreqAI target indicators flagged in the biased-indicators column are not biased. (low confidence) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/lookahead-analysis/ · keywords: Crypto bot strategy drift and shadow divergence monitoring

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Design inference: investigate simulation, data, timing, and venue differences before classifying live-versus-shadow divergence as signal decay. QuantConnect documents modeling and fill discrepancies; NautilusTrader explicitly warns that shared strategy code does not reproduce all live-system behavior. (medium confidence) — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/live-trading/reconciliation · keywords: Crypto bot strategy drift and shadow divergence monitoring · also: https://nautilustrader.io/docs/latest/concepts/live/
- [statement] FreqAI documentation describes sequential pair training that creates unequal model ages, and periodic retraining in dry/live deployment. Model age therefore needs per-pair interpretation rather than a single bot-wide freshness assumption. (low confidence) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/freqai-running/ · keywords: Crypto bot strategy drift and shadow divergence monitoring
- [statement] In Freqtrade issue 7248, a maintainer suggested inadequate resampled history as a possible cause of backtest/dry-run mismatch: backtests had the whole interval, while live data arrived in bounded candle histories. The comment explicitly called the explanation an assumption, so it is a diagnostic hypothesis rather than a confirmed general cause. (low confidence) — https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/issues/7248 · keywords: Crypto bot strategy drift and shadow divergence monitoring
- [statement] Proof Trading describes persisting a sequenced event stream and replaying it through production code inside a debugger to inspect unexpected decisions. Its reproducibility argument depends on deterministic nodes using only sequenced inputs, including time; it is an engineering pattern for diagnosis rather than evidence of profitable crypto strategies. (low confidence) — https://medium.com/prooftrading/proof-engineering-the-algorithmic-trading-platform-b9c2f195433d · keywords: Crypto bot strategy drift and shadow divergence monitoring
- [statement] FreqAI describes the Dissimilarity Index as a measure of prediction uncertainty based on distance from training feature vectors. A higher `DI_threshold` permits more extrapolation; a lower threshold discards more predictions. This is a feature-space novelty signal, rather than documented proof that the strategy has lost profitability. (low confidence) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/freqai-feature-engineering/ · keywords: Crypto bot strategy drift and shadow divergence monitoring
- [statement] FreqAI requires a new `identifier` when features change so that it trains new models instead of reusing cached backtest predictions. A feature change and an entry/exit threshold change have different model-reuse implications. (low confidence) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/freqai-running/ · keywords: Crypto bot strategy drift and shadow divergence monitoring

## Facts and statements

- [statement] QuantConnect describes parallel out-of-sample backtests and overlaid live/backtest equity curves as a way to measure execution-mode divergence. Curve deviations show a difference between modes; the documentation says several factors can contribute. (low confidence) — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/live-trading/reconciliation · keywords: Crypto bot strategy drift and shadow divergence monitoring
- [statement] FreqAI warns that its continual-learning implementation is experimental and can overfit or become stuck in local minima as the market moves away from the model. Enabling continual learning alone is therefore not evidence that drift has been controlled. (low confidence) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/freqai-running/ · keywords: Crypto bot strategy drift and shadow divergence monitoring
- [statement] The FreqAI running-models page uses two different expiry-setting names: its live-deployment paragraph says expired_hours, while its model-expiration section and configuration example say expiration_hours. These passages do not establish which setting an installed version accepts. (low confidence) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/freqai-running/ · keywords: Crypto bot strategy drift and shadow divergence monitoring
- [statement] An October 2026 NautilusTrader RFC reports that adding to a position could grow resting reduce-only orders in backtests beyond submitted quantity, changing scale-out behavior relative to the venue behavior described by its author. The author measured this on named pre-release builds and raised a design proposal; this does not establish a released fix or all-venue behavior. (low confidence) — https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/issues/5348 · keywords: Crypto bot strategy drift and shadow divergence monitoring
- [statement] Kiploks recommends comparing live results with research and rolling walk-forward baselines, monitoring trade frequency and partial fills, separating execution drift from signal drift, and defining pause rules before losses. These are attributed monitoring suggestions; the article supplies no validated universal alert threshold. (low confidence) — https://kiploks.com/research/regime-change-detection-for-trading-bots-when-market-conditions-shift · keywords: Crypto bot strategy drift and shadow divergence monitoring
- [statement] Freqtrade describes lookahead-analysis as comparing baseline and sliced backtests for changed indicator values and shifted entries/exits. This scopes a divergence investigation: future-information leakage in a backtest must be checked alongside deployment-time strategy drift. (low confidence) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/lookahead-analysis/ · keywords: Crypto bot strategy drift and shadow divergence monitoring
- [statement] Monitoring inference: investigate data availability and execution assumptions before attributing live/backtest divergence to strategy decay. QuantConnect identifies data and fill-model differences, while Freqtrade explains that future-data leakage can inflate backtests. (medium confidence) — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/live-trading/reconciliation · keywords: Crypto bot strategy drift and shadow divergence monitoring · also: https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/lookahead-analysis/
- [statement] FreqAI stores predictions associated with a model identifier in `historic_predictions.pkl` and documents `--freqai-backtest-live-models` to reuse live historic predictions in backtesting for comparison or study. This provides a documented input for retrospective shadow comparison. (low confidence) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/freqai-running/ · keywords: Crypto bot strategy drift and shadow divergence monitoring
- [statement] FreqAI documents sequential per-pair training and consequent differences in model ages. Its model-expiration section uses `expiration_hours` to restrict predictions to sufficiently recent models; model age is therefore a separate monitoring dimension from trade outcomes. (low confidence) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/freqai-running/ · keywords: Crypto bot strategy drift and shadow divergence monitoring
- [statement] Freqtrade lookahead-analysis compares a baseline backtest with separate verification backtests for entry and exit signals and reports changed dataframe values. It is a diagnostic for information leakage, not a live-market drift detector. (low confidence) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/lookahead-analysis/ · keywords: Crypto bot strategy drift and shadow divergence monitoring

## Research summary — Crypto bot strategy drift and shadow divergence monitoring

Strategy-drift monitoring compares deployed decisions and behavior against research or shadow expectations while investigating execution-mode differences. The evidence covers parallel out-of-sample reconciliation, operational state checks, per-pair model freshness, replay-based diagnosis, lookahead checks, and historical mismatch reports. Divergence needs attribution before it is treated as signal decay: data history, prediction reloads, timing, and simulation behavior can differ. Monitoring and pause suggestions are distinguished from validated thresholds, and an internal documentation conflict over expiry configuration remains unresolved.
